newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Arabs wounded by Israeli settler in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Two Arabs wounded by Israeli settler in West Bank.

text.p: A Jewish settler shot and wounded two Palestinians on Monday in West Bank violence coinciding with a crisis visit to Washington by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"An Israeli car was passing in the Ramallah area and stones were thrown at it. A man who was inside the car opened fire and as a result two Palestinians were injured, one seriously and the other lightly," said Israeli police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin.
Officials at Ramallah hospital, north of Jerusalem, confirmed that one Palestinian was wounded in the chest. They had no information about a second wounded man.
"The police are at the scene. The car is not there and its identity is not known to the police," Menuhin said.
A Jewish settler spokesman confirmed the shooting and said it was the result of "massive stone-throwing on an Israeli car."
The West Bank and Gaza Strip have been rocked by daily unrest since Israel broke ground on March 18 for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Three Palestinians have been killed by Israeli gunfire and scores wounded in the violence.
Netanyahu was due to meet President Bill Clinton later in the day as part of a U.S. attempt to rescue the Israeli-Palestinian peace process.

Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, who returned on Sunday from talks with top U.S. officials in Washington, said a closure which Israel tightened in the West Bank and Gaza after a March 21 suicide bombing in Tel Aviv would continue.

"Closure is not a goal but a means...it is entirely clear to us that the fact of closure raises the level of violence -- stone-throwing and petrol bombs -- in the territories of Judea, Samaria and Gaza," Mordechai told reporters.
Some 130,000 Jewish settlers live amidst more than two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
